title: Non-interactive mode: print, JSON output, pipes
goal: `centcom -p "prompt"` runs one task without a TUI by driving an engine (`claude-code` or `codex`) and prints the result as text, JSON or stream-JSON of Centcom's normalised events, composes with pipes and stdin, supports resume flags and exits with predictable codes, with no new authentication.
scope_in: Flags in `apps/cli/src/print/`: `-p, --print [prompt]`, `--engine claude-code|codex` (default from config `engine.default`, else the first engine reported installed and signed in), `--output-format text|json|stream-json` (default `text`), `--input-format text|stream-json`, `--model <name>` (lane C028), `--resume <id>`, `--continue`/`-c` (lane C026), `--max-turns <n>` (default 50), `--timeout <seconds>`, `--permission-mode <ask|accept-edits|plan>`, `--allow <rule>` (repeatable, syntax of lane C015), `--cwd <dir>`.
Prompt sources: argument, else piped stdin (`cat log | centcom -p "explain"` appends stdin as a fenced block; cap 1 MiB, over cap exits 2 with `Input is too large (max 1 MiB).`).

Output: `text` streams assistant text to stdout only; `json` prints one final object `{type:'result', is_error, result, usage, session_id, engine, duration_ms}` where `usage` is what the engine reported (tokens, `cost_usd_estimate` when reported) and `session_id` is the Centcom session id; `stream-json` prints one JSON object per line using Centcom's NORMALISED event names (`session.started`, `text.delta`, `text.done`, `tool.requested`, `tool.result`, `approval.requested`, `usage.report`, `turn.done`, `error`), ending with the same `result` line. Raw CLI output is never passed through.
stdout carries data only; progress, warnings and logs go to stderr; no colour, spinner, mascot or alt screen when not a TTY or with `NO_COLOR`.

Non-interactive permissions: nothing is prompted; approvals are answered by the policy of lane C015 from `--permission-mode`/`--allow`, else denied; if any were denied the process exits 3 after finishing.

Exit codes in `exit-codes.ts`: 0 success, 1 general failure, 2 usage error, 3 permission denied, 4 provider not installed or not signed in (`provider_not_installed`, `provider_not_signed_in`, `provider_policy_blocked`, `provider_method_disabled`), 5 plan or rate limit (`provider_cap_reached`, `provider_rate_limited`, CT-ERR 429-class), 6 network/unavailable or engine protocol error (`provider_protocol_error`, `provider_version_unsupported`, 5xx), 124 timeout, 130 interrupted (via lane C030).

JSON error output: on failure in JSON modes the final line is `{type:'result', is_error:true, error:{code, message, retry_after_s?, request_id?}}` where `code` is a CT-ERR code or a client-local provider error code of CT-PROVIDER section 9, and `message` is the engine's own text verbatim (redacted by lane C005).
scope_out: Interactive TUI (lanes C034-C049) and first-run flows.
Login and provider setup: print mode only reports `provider_not_signed_in` with exit 4 and points to `centcom provider login` (lane C104); no new auth, no keys read.
Engine adapters, the runner and the policy engine (lanes C013, C102, C103, C015).
Joining or hosting multiplayer sessions (session lanes).
build_against: The fake-CLI replay of golden transcripts from `contracts/fixtures/providers/` behind the engine adapters (or a stub `AgentEngine`), the in-memory bus of lane C025, and CLI tests that spawn the built binary with the pipe harness of lane C008. Error cases use CT-ERR problem+json fixtures and CT-PROVIDER error codes. No real CLI, no backend.
interfaces: `runPrint(deps: {engines: EngineRegistry; runner: AgentRunner; bus: EventBus; io: {stdin: NodeJS.ReadStream; stdout: NodeJS.WriteStream; stderr: NodeJS.WriteStream}; clock: Clock; errors: ErrorMapper; sessions: SessionStore}, opts: PrintOptions): Promise<number>` (returns exit code; never calls `process.exit`)

`type PrintOptions = {prompt?: string; engine?: 'claude-code'|'codex'; outputFormat: 'text'|'json'|'stream-json'; inputFormat: 'text'|'stream-json'; model?: string; resume?: string; continue?: boolean; maxTurns: number; timeoutS?: number; permissionMode?: string; allow: string[]; cwd?: string}`
`exitCodeFor(err: unknown): number` and constant table `EXIT_CODES`; `formatResult(r: PrintResult, fmt: 'json'|'stream-json'): string`
acceptance: `centcom -p "hi" --engine claude-code` against the fake CLI prints only the assistant text plus a newline on stdout, nothing on stderr except warnings, exit 0; the same with `--engine codex` prints the same text from the Codex golden transcript.
`--output-format json` prints exactly one line of valid JSON with `type:'result'`, `is_error:false`, `engine`, `usage` as reported, and `session_id` matching `^ses_`; `| jq .result` works.

`--output-format stream-json` prints one JSON object per line using only the normalised event names listed above plus the final `result`; every line parses, no raw CLI event (`system/init`, JSON-RPC frames) appears.
`echo data | centcom -p summarize` includes stdin in the prompt; 2 MiB stdin exits 2 with the documented message and no engine is started.

An approval with no `--allow` rule is denied, the run continues and the exit code is 3; with `--permission-mode accept-edits` an edit approval passes and exit is 0; there is no flag that approves everything.

`--resume <id>` starts the engine with the stored engine session id (asserted from the fake CLI's argv: `--resume <session_id>` for Claude Code, `exec resume` for Codex); `--continue` with no stored session exits 1 with `No session to continue in this directory.`.

Fake CLI reports `provider_not_signed_in` -> exit 4; `provider_cap_reached` with text `usage limit reached` -> exit 5, JSON `error.code:'provider_cap_reached'` and `error.message` equal to the CLI's text, text mode writes it to stderr.

SIGINT stops the run via lane C030 and exits 130 with a final `result` line `is_error:true` in JSON modes; `--timeout 5` with a stuck engine exits 124 at 5 s (+/-200 ms fake clock); `| head -1` stops the engine within 1 s with no EPIPE stack.
With stdout not a TTY or `NO_COLOR=1` no ESC bytes appear; no output line contains any `must_match` string of `secret-patterns.json` even when the engine echoes one.
tests: print/text-json.test.ts: formats for success and failure on both engines.
print/stream-json.test.ts: line schema, allow-list of normalised names, ordering, final result.
print/stdin.test.ts: pipe input, cap, empty prompt, TTY with no prompt exits 2.
print/resume.test.ts: resume and continue flags per engine.
print/exit-codes.test.ts: table-driven mapping of CT-ERR and provider codes.
print/signals.test.ts: SIGINT, SIGTERM, timeout, EPIPE; redaction of output.
guardrails: MUST write only machine-readable data to stdout in JSON modes; human text goes to stderr.
MUST NOT approve anything implicitly and MUST NOT read, accept or print any credential; auth problems are reported with exit 4 and the vendor's `login` hint only.
MUST map exit codes from error `code` values (CT-ERR or CT-PROVIDER section 9), never from message text; unknown codes map by status class else exit 1.
MUST pass engine error text through the redaction helper of lane C005 before printing, verbatim otherwise.
MUST NOT call `process.exit` in library code; MUST bound memory (stdin 1 MiB, lines over 1 MiB truncated with `truncated:true`).
MUST NOT import vendor SDKs; all model-facing work is the engine child process.
failure_modes: Missing prompt and stdin is a TTY -> exit 2 with a one-line usage message, no engine started.
Engine crashes or emits unparsable output before any result -> final `result` line `is_error:true`, `error.code:'provider_protocol_error'`, exit 6.
Stdout closed early (EPIPE) -> interrupt via lane C030 and exit 0 silently.
Requested engine not installed -> exit 4 with `provider_not_installed` and the install hint of lane C104's table.
notes: Output no longer mirrors Claude Code's own stream-json; it is Centcom's normalised stream so scripts do not change when a CLI changes. Event names must match lane C101.
